description:
Run JavaScript in a persistent computer-use session. Put a whole step in one call: several actions, then one read. Top-level const/let/function/await persist across calls until js_reset (redeclaring is fine).

const calc = await ui.getApp("Calculator");   // name, bundle id, or "pid:123"; launches if needed, does not steal focus
await calc.pressKey("Escape");                 // xdotool syntax: Return, Tab, ctrl+a, super+c (super = Cmd)
await calc.typeText("12*3=");                  // "\n" presses Return
await calc.getAXState();                       // text accessibility tree; later reads return only changes

Reads: getAXState({disableDiffing, frames, menus, window}) returns "<index> <role> \"label\" value=..." lines. frames:true adds @x,y wxh in image pixels. Every read emits its output; pass {emit:false} to just get the value. app.find({role, label, id, text}) and app.nodes() return elements as data without printing; app.text(i) gives a field's full text; app.expect(query) checks a step and stops the call with the window shown if it fails; app.scrollTo(query) scrolls until an element shows.
Token cost, cheapest first: find()/nodes()/text() (data, nothing printed) < getAXState() diff < app.ocr() (text with clickable @x,y frames, also diffed on repeat) < getScreenshot() (an image, by far the most expensive). When a read shows only one or two elements (remote desktops, virtual machines, canvases, games), the screen is drawn, not described: use app.ocr(), not screenshots. Take a screenshot only to judge layout or visuals that text cannot convey. To collect text from a long list, loop scroll + ocr({emit:false}) inside one call and return only the text you need.
Actions: click(target, {button, count, modifiers}), doubleClick, rightClick, scroll(target, dy), drag(from, to), setValue(index, v), focus(index), selectText(index, {start, length}), performSecondaryAction(index, "Show Menu"), listActions(index), activate(), windows(), frame(index), center(index).
A target is an element index from the tree, or [x, y] pixels in the window image (same space as the screenshot and frames). Prefer indices; when the tree has nothing useful, click the [x, y] center of an ocr() frame. Input stays in the background (focus and the user's cursor don't move); if an action fails, retry it once with {window: <title>} before passing {foreground: true}, and only for the step that needs it.
ui.listApps() lists running apps. console.log adds text to the result. help() or help("click") prints the full API. If a result says "Stopped:" the user took over (switched apps or pressed Escape): stop and ask before continuing.

code.description: JavaScript to run. Top-level await is supported.
